subjects.name: Deutsch
subjects.description: Core subject from Klasse 1 to the Abitur: daily in primary school and about four to five lessons a week at the Gymnasium. It covers learning to read and write, spelling, writing, reading, literature and media, and reflection on language, anchored on the KMK Bildungsstandards (Primarbereich and ESA/MSA 2022, Allgemeine Hochschulreife 2012). Deutsch is compulsory until the Abitur and is taken as a Grundkurs or Leistungskurs in the Qualifikationsphase, where literary history, interpretation and reflection on language come to the fore.

topics.name: Word Classes Overview

topics.description: Sort all word classes into one system: inflecting words (the verb is conjugated; noun, article, adjective and pronoun are declined) and non-inflecting words (adverb, preposition, conjunction, interjection), using the Wortartenbaum as the reference model for grammar in secondary school.
evidence: Classify every word of a sentence by word class
Test whether a word can be conjugated, declined or not changed at all
Complete a word-class tree (Wortartenbaum)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is given the sentence 'Gestern lief der kleine Hund schnell über die Straße', can they name the word class of every word and say which ones can change their form?

prerequisites.reason: Nouns are the first declinable word class
Verbs are the conjugable word class
Adjectives belong to the declinable words

osMatches.note: os covers conjunctions, prepositions and interjections only

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern requires the Latin terms (incl. Numerale, Subjunktion) in Jgst. 5; NRW lists seven word classes for the Erprobungsstufe and adds Präposition and Interjektion in Kl. 7/8.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Adverbs
topics.description: Recognise adverbs as non-inflecting words that specify time, place, manner or reason (gestern, dort, gern, deshalb) and distinguish them from adjectives, which can be declined (der schnelle Läufer) even when they describe a verb (Er läuft schnell).
evidence: Find adverbs of time, place, manner and reason in a text
Show by declension that 'schnell' is an adjective but 'gern' an adverb
Use adverbs such as deshalb or trotzdem to link sentences
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees 'Sie singt gern und laut', can they explain why 'gern' is an adverb but 'laut' counts as an adjective in German grammar?

prerequisites.reason: Adverbs are learned in contrast to adjectives
Many adverbs answer Wann? and Wo?

osMatches.note: English adverbs often carry -ly; German adverbially used adjectives stay adjectives

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Strong and Weak Verbs
topics.description: Distinguish weak verbs (spielen – spielte – gespielt) from strong verbs with a vowel change (singen – sang – gesungen) and mixed verbs (bringen – brachte – gebracht), and form the three principal parts (Infinitiv, Präteritum, Partizip II) needed to build all tenses.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Future Perfect (Futur II)
topics.description: Form the Futur II with werden + Partizip II + haben/sein (Morgen werde ich den Aufsatz geschrieben haben) and use it for actions completed by a point in the future or for assumptions about the past (Er wird den Bus verpasst haben), completing the system of six German tenses.

Name all six tenses of a given verb

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Using Tenses Consistently
topics.description: Choose tenses deliberately in own texts: keep the Präteritum as the narrative tense, mark earlier events with the Plusquamperfekt, use the Präsens for summaries and descriptions, and avoid unmotivated switches of tense.

Mark earlier events with the Plusquamperfekt (Nachdem er gegessen hatte, …)
Find and correct tense switches in a text

prerequisites.reason: Choice between narrative and present tense
Tense errors are found while revising

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Active and Passive Voice
topics.description: Form the werden-passive in different tenses (Das Haus wird gebaut / wurde gebaut / ist gebaut worden), transform active sentences into passive ones and back, and explain the effect: the passive puts the action in focus and can leave out who does it.

Add or leave out the agent with von
Explain why reports and instructions often use the passive
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} turns 'Der Hausmeister öffnet das Tor' into the passive, do they write 'Das Tor wird (vom Hausmeister) geöffnet' and can they say why one might leave out the Hausmeister?

The accusative object becomes the subject
The subject changes between active and passive

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Predicative Complements
topics.description: Recognise the Prädikativ as the part of the predicate that follows copula verbs such as sein, werden, bleiben and heißen — a noun in the nominative (Sie wird Ärztin) or an adjective (Er bleibt ruhig) — and distinguish it from an accusative object.
evidence: Identify the Prädikativ after sein, werden and bleiben
Explain why 'Ärztin' in 'Sie wird Ärztin' is not an object
Use the nominative correctly in the Prädikativ (Er ist ein guter Freund)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} analyses 'Mein Bruder ist ein guter Koch', can they explain that 'ein guter Koch' is a Prädikativ in the nominative, not an object?

prerequisites.reason: It must be distinguished from objects

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Attributes in Noun Phrases
topics.description: Recognise attributes as parts of a Satzglied that describe a noun more precisely — adjective attribute (der alte Turm), genitive attribute (der Turm der Burg), prepositional attribute (der Turm mit der Glocke) and apposition — and show with the Umstellprobe that they move together with their noun.
evidence: Mark the attributes in a noun phrase and name their kind
Show with the Umstellprobe that an attribute is not a separate Satzglied
Expand plain noun phrases with attributes for more precise descriptions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} moves 'das Fahrrad meines Bruders mit dem roten Sattel' around in a sentence, do they see that it is one Satzglied and can they name the two attributes?

prerequisites.reason: Attributes are identified with the Umstellprobe
Adjective attributes are the simplest kind
Genitive attributes need correct case forms

osMatches.note: English expanded noun phrases; German adds genitive attributes

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Prepositional and Genitive Objects
topics.description: Identify the prepositional object, whose preposition is fixed by the verb (warten auf, sich freuen über), and the rare genitive object (gedenken, sich annehmen), and distinguish a prepositional object from an adverbial by the question test (Worauf wartest du? vs. Wo wartest du?).
evidence: Ask the right question for a prepositional object (Worüber? Woran?)
Distinguish 'Ich warte auf den Bus' (object) from 'Ich warte an der Haltestelle' (adverbial)
List verbs that take a fixed preposition
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares 'Sie denkt an die Ferien' with 'Sie sitzt an dem Tisch', can they explain which phrase is an object and which an adverbial?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Compound vs Complex Sentences
topics.description: Distinguish the Satzreihe (main clauses joined by und, aber, denn, oder or without a conjunction) from the Satzgefüge (main clause plus subordinate clause with the verb at the end), using the position of the finite verb and the kind of conjunction (coordinating vs. subordinating).
evidence: Classify sentences as Satzreihe or Satzgefüge
Sort conjunctions into coordinating and subordinating
Rewrite a Satzreihe as a Satzgefüge (denn → weil) and notice the verb moving
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares 'Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn es regnet' with '…, weil es regnet', can they explain why only the second is a Satzgefüge?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on main and subordinate clauses
The conjunction decides the sentence type
Verb position is the key test

osMatches.note: os: simple, compound and complex sentences in English

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Adverbial Clauses
topics.nameDe: Adverbialsätze: temporal, kausal, final, konditional, konzessiv
topics.description: Identify subordinate clauses that work as adverbials and name their meaning relation from the conjunction — temporal (als, nachdem), causal (weil, da), final (damit), conditional (wenn, falls), concessive (obwohl), consecutive (sodass) — and use them to express logical relations precisely.
evidence: Name the meaning relation of an adverbial clause
Replace an adverbial (wegen des Regens) with an adverbial clause (weil es regnet)
Choose the conjunction that fits the intended relation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads 'Obwohl sie müde war, lernte sie weiter', can they say that it is a concessive clause and explain the difference from 'Weil sie müde war, …'?

osMatches.note: os: expressing time, place and cause with conjunctions

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: temporal, causal, final and modal clauses in Jgst. 6, conditional, consecutive and concessive relations in Jgst. 7; NRW: Adverbialsatz in Kl. 7/8.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Latin Grammar Terminology
topics.description: Use the Latin-based grammar terms of secondary school (Nomen/Substantiv, Verb, Adverb, Nominativ to Akkusativ, Präsens, Präteritum, Subjekt, Prädikat, Objekt) instead of primary-school German terms (Namenwort, Tuwort, Wer-Fall) and use them to talk precisely about language.
evidence: Match primary-school terms to their Latin equivalents
Describe a sentence using only the Latin terms
Use the terms when comparing German with English or Latin
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears 'Bestimme das Prädikat und das Akkusativobjekt', do they know what is meant without asking for the German terms?

osMatches.note: os: language terminology for English

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern requires the Latin terms from Jgst. 5; elsewhere they are introduced gradually, often in step with Latin as a second foreign language.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Types of Word Formation
topics.nameDe: Wortbildung: Zusammensetzung, Ableitung, Grund- und Bestimmungswort
topics.description: Distinguish the main word-formation processes — composition (Haus + Tür), derivation with prefixes and suffixes (Freund → freundlich) and conversion (laufen → das Laufen) — and analyse compounds into Grundwort (it decides word class and gender) and Bestimmungswort, including linking elements (Fugen-s: Liebesbrief).
evidence: Name the formation type of a given word
Explain why 'die Haustür' is feminine and 'der Türgriff' masculine
Find the linking element in compounds such as Geburtstag
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees 'Zeitungsartikel', can they split it into Bestimmungswort, Fugen-s and Grundwort and say why it is 'der' Artikel?

osMatches.note: os: converting words into verbs in English

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Superordinate and Subordinate Terms
topics.description: Order words in hierarchies of superordinate and subordinate terms (Fahrzeug – Auto – Cabrio), use Oberbegriffe to summarise and Unterbegriffe to write precisely, and use the relation for definitions (Ein Cabrio ist ein Auto, das …).
evidence: Build a three-level word hierarchy
Replace a vague Oberbegriff with a precise Unterbegriff in a text
Write a definition with Oberbegriff and distinguishing feature
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has to define 'Rose', do they start with an Oberbegriff (eine Blume, die …) and add what makes it special?

prerequisites.reason: Word fields are ordered into hierarchies

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Working Out Word Meanings
topics.description: Work out the meaning of unknown words in a text from the context, from the word's parts (Wortbildung) and by checking a print or online dictionary, choosing the meaning that fits when a word has several.
evidence: Infer a meaning from the surrounding sentences and check it
Use word parts to guess a meaning (unübersichtlich)
Choose the fitting meaning from a dictionary entry with several senses
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} meets an unknown word like 'beharrlich' in a text, do they first guess from context and word parts and then check the dictionary?

prerequisites.reason: Decoding long words via syllables and morphemes
Dictionary lookup is one of the methods
Words with several meanings need context

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Similar-Sounding Words
topics.nameDe: Gleich und ähnlich klingende Wörter (seid/seit, wieder/wider)
topics.description: Spell words that sound the same or almost the same but are written differently according to meaning or origin — seid/seit, wieder (noch einmal)/wider (gegen), end-/ent-, tot/Tod, Lid/Lied, Stadt/statt — using meaning tests and word families.
evidence: Decide between wieder and wider with the meaning test
Use the word family to choose tot or Tod
Correct mix-ups in a dictation text
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes 'Ihr seit spät dran', can they correct it to 'seid' and explain the difference from 'seit gestern'?

osMatches.note: English homophones; the German pairs differ

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Commas Around Insertions
topics.nameDe: Komma bei Apposition, nachgestellten Erläuterungen und Einschüben
topics.description: Enclose appositions (Herr Schmidt, unser Trainer, kommt), added explanations (Er isst gern Obst, besonders Äpfel) and inserted remarks (Parenthese) with commas on both sides — or with dashes or brackets — unless the sentence ends there.
evidence: Set paired commas around an apposition in the middle of a sentence
Mark added explanations introduced by besonders, vor allem, und zwar
Choose between commas, dashes and brackets for an insertion
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes 'Mein Onkel ein Bäcker steht früh auf', do they add the two commas around 'ein Bäcker'?

prerequisites.reason: The apposition is a kind of attribute
Paired commas also enclose embedded clauses

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Capitalising Times of Day
topics.nameDe: Groß- und Kleinschreibung von Zeitangaben (heute Abend, abends)
topics.description: Apply the rules for times of day and weekdays: nouns after time adverbs are capitalised (heute Abend, gestern Morgen, am Montag), adverbs ending in -s are written in lower case (abends, montags), and fixed phrases follow the noun signal (eines Tages).
evidence: Write 'heute Abend' and 'abends' correctly
Explain the -s rule for montags and nachts
Correct the capitalisation of time expressions in a text
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes 'Wir treffen uns morgen abend und spielen samstags Fußball', can they correct it to 'morgen Abend' and explain why 'samstags' stays lower case?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Reading a Dictionary Entry
topics.description: Use a print or online dictionary (Duden, DWDS) as an information source beyond spelling: read the abbreviations in an entry for gender, genitive and plural, principal parts of verbs, hyphenation, meanings, usage labels (ugs., veraltet) and origin.
evidence: Read gender, genitive and plural from an entry
Find the principal parts and the hyphenation of a verb
Explain usage labels such as umgangssprachlich
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks up 'Kaktus' in the Duden, can they find the gender and the two possible plural forms in the entry?

osMatches.note: os: dictionary use for spelling; German entries add grammatical data

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Writing Stories by Genre Patterns
topics.nameDe: Nach literarischen Mustern erzählen (Fabel, Märchen, Lügengeschichte)
topics.description: Write an own story that follows the pattern of a known genre — a fable with animals and a lesson, a fairy tale with fixed formulas and magic, a tall tale (Lügengeschichte in the style of Münchhausen) or a legend — deliberately using the genre's typical features.
evidence: List the pattern features before writing
Write a complete fable whose lesson follows from the plot
Check the own story against a list of genre features
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked to write a new fable, does their story have animals with typical traits, a short conflict with a twist and a lesson at the end?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW Klassenarbeit type 1 includes 'auf der Basis von Materialien oder Mustern erzählen'.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Summarising a Story's Plot
topics.description: Divide a story into meaningful sections, note the key action of each in one short sentence and join these into a brief, factual summary in the present tense — the step that prepares the formal Inhaltsangabe.
evidence: Divide a story into sections (Sinnabschnitte) with headings
Write one sentence per plot step in the Präsens
Leave out details, feelings and direct speech in the summary
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} summarises a short story they have read, do they give the main steps in order, in the present tense and without retelling every detail?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Informative Writing from Materials
topics.nameDe: Informierenden Text auf Grundlage von Materialien schreiben
topics.description: Write an informative text (e.g. an article for the school newspaper or an encyclopedia entry) from several given materials — short texts, tables, diagrams, pictures: select the relevant information, order it logically and put it into own words for a defined audience.
evidence: Select the information relevant for the task from three or more materials
Turn diagram data into sentences
Structure the text with introduction, ordered main part and conclusion
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets a text, a table and a diagram about plastic waste, can they write an informative article in their own words that uses all three sensibly?

prerequisites.reason: Data from tables and charts are used
The materials have to be understood first

topics.laenderNotes: NRW requires Klassenarbeit type 2 (informierendes Schreiben, also material-based) from the Erprobungsstufe; Bayern asks for material-based informative texts from Jgst. 7.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Literary Fairy Tales
topics.description: Distinguish folk tales, passed on orally and collected by the Brothers Grimm, from literary fairy tales (Kunstmärchen) written by a known author such as Wilhelm Hauff or Hans Christian Andersen, which are longer, more detailed and often end unhappily.
evidence: Name three differences between Volksmärchen and Kunstmärchen
Assign tales to the two kinds with reasons
Compare the ending and style of a Grimm tale with an Andersen tale
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares 'Rotkäppchen' with Andersen's 'Die kleine Meerjungfrau', can they explain why the second is a Kunstmärchen?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Reading a Youth Novel
topics.nameDe: Einen Kinder- oder Jugendroman als Ganzschrift erschließen
topics.description: Work through a whole children's or young-adult novel (Ganzschrift) in class: keep track of the plot across chapters, map the characters and their relationships in a Figurenkonstellation, follow the main conflict and relate the book's themes to own experience.

Summarise the plot development chapter by chapter
State and justify a personal judgement of the book
topics.assessmentPrompt: After reading a youth novel in class, can {{name}} draw how the main characters are related and explain how the central conflict develops and is resolved?

prerequisites.reason: A reading journal accompanies the book

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Rhyme Schemes
topics.description: Mark the rhyme scheme of a poem with letters (aabb, abab, abba), name the forms Paarreim, Kreuzreim, umarmender Reim and Schweifreim, and notice impure rhymes (Freude – Weide).
evidence: Mark the rhyme scheme of a stanza with letters
Name Paarreim, Kreuzreim and umarmender Reim
Write a stanza in a given rhyme scheme
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets a stanza ending 'Haus – Maus – Wald – kalt', can they mark it 'aabb' and call it a Paarreim?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on rhyme, line and stanza

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Metre in Poems
topics.description: Find stressed and unstressed syllables in lines of verse, mark them and identify the metre — Jambus (x X), Trochäus (X x), Daktylus (X x x), Anapäst (x x X) — and the number of stresses, and describe how the metre shapes the rhythm of a poem.
evidence: Mark the stressed syllables in a line of verse
Name the metre of a regular poem
Count the stresses per line (e.g. vierhebiger Jambus)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads 'Der Mond ist aufgegangen' aloud, can they mark the stresses and name the metre as Jambus?

prerequisites.reason: Formal analysis of poems starts with rhyme

topics.laenderNotes: Baden-Württemberg and NRW name Metrum for Kl. 5/6; many schools practise the terms systematically only in Kl. 7/8 with the ballad.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: The Speaker in a Poem
topics.nameDe: Lyrisches Ich und Sprechsituation im Gedicht
topics.description: Distinguish the speaker of a poem (lyrisches Ich or lyrischer Sprecher) from the real poet and describe the speaking situation: who speaks, to whom, in which situation and in what mood.
evidence: Explain why the lyrisches Ich is not simply the author
Describe who speaks to whom in a poem
Name the speaker's mood with evidence from the text
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads a poem in which an 'ich' is afraid of the dark, can they explain that this speaker need not be the poet and describe the situation?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Reading Dramatic Scenes
topics.description: Read short plays and scenes as a text type of their own: recognise dialogue, monologue, stage directions (Regieanweisungen) and scene divisions, and work out the characters' intentions and how a conflict develops from what they say.
evidence: Distinguish spoken text from stage directions
Describe what each character wants in a scene
Trace how a quarrel builds up in a dialogue
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads a short scene, can they say what the stage directions tell the actors and what each character wants from the other?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Camera Shots and Angles
topics.description: Name the main shot sizes (Totale, Halbtotale, Nahaufnahme, Detail) and camera angles (Normalsicht, Vogel- and Froschperspektive) in film and describe their effect, e.g. a low angle making a character seem powerful.
evidence: Identify shot sizes in film stills
Name the camera angle and its effect
Plan a short storyboard with chosen shots
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a scene filmed from below a character, can they name the Froschperspektive and explain what it suggests about the character?

prerequisites.reason: Comparing book and film introduces camera work
Media analysis starts with audio and video media

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Pro and Contra Discussion
topics.description: Prepare an assigned position for a structured pro-and-contra discussion (e.g. a mobile phone ban at school), collect arguments with examples, anticipate counter-arguments, respond to the other side in turn and summarise the outcome.

Respond directly to a counter-argument
Summarise both positions fairly at the end
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a class pro-and-contra discussion, does {{name}} back up their side with reasons and examples and react to what the other side has just said?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Subjunctive I Forms
topics.description: Form the Konjunktiv I from the infinitive stem (er sage, sie habe, es sei, sie werde kommen) for present, past (er habe gesagt, sie sei gegangen) and future, and recognise it as the mood of reported speech in newspapers and formal texts.

Form the past Konjunktiv I (habe gesagt, sei gegangen)
Recognise Konjunktiv I forms in a news article
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked for the Konjunktiv I of 'er kommt', 'sie hat' and 'es ist', can they give 'er komme', 'sie habe' and 'es sei'?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Subjunctive II

Write unreal conditional sentences about the present and the past
Turn a direct request into a polite one with the Konjunktiv II
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to say that they would have come if they had known, can they produce 'Wenn ich es gewusst hätte, wäre ich gekommen'?

osMatches.note: English subjunctive and unreal conditionals

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Reported Speech
topics.nameDe: Indirekte Rede mit Konjunktiv I und Ersatzformen
topics.description: Turn direct speech into indirect speech: introduce it with a verb of saying, shift pronouns and references to time and place, use the Konjunktiv I and switch to Konjunktiv II or würde where the Konjunktiv I looks like the indicative (sie haben → sie hätten).
evidence: Rewrite a dialogue as indirect speech with correct pronoun shifts
Use the substitute form when the Konjunktiv I equals the indicative
Report questions and commands (ob …, er solle …)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reports 'Wir haben morgen keine Zeit', do they write 'Sie sagten, sie hätten am nächsten Tag keine Zeit'?

Direct speech is the starting point

osMatches.note: English reported speech uses backshift; German uses the Konjunktiv

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Ways of Reporting Speech
topics.description: Use the full range of ways to report what others said — indirect speech, paraphrase, dass-clauses, modal verbs (soll, will), phrases such as laut, zufolge, nach Angaben — and choose them to show distance from or agreement with the source.

Use 'soll' and 'will' to signal distance
Mark adopted statements clearly in a summary or analysis
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reports a politician's claim, can they use 'Laut Minister …' or 'Er will … haben' and explain what each form signals?

prerequisites.reason: Indirect speech is one of the forms

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: State Passive and Passive Alternatives
topics.description: Distinguish the werden-passive (Die Tür wird geschlossen — a process) from the sein-passive (Die Tür ist geschlossen — a resulting state), use passive alternatives (man, sich lassen, -bar, sein + zu) and judge which form suits a text.
evidence: Classify passive sentences as Vorgangs- or Zustandspassiv
Replace the passive with man, lassen or -bar
Justify the choice of active or passive in a factual text
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares 'Das Museum wird geöffnet' and 'Das Museum ist geöffnet', can they explain the difference between process and state?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Clauses as Sentence Parts
topics.nameDe: Gliedsätze: Subjekt-, Objekt-, Adverbial- und Attributsatz
topics.description: Determine the function of a subordinate clause in the whole sentence: it can replace the subject (Wer zu spät kommt, …), an object (Ich hoffe, dass …) or an adverbial (Als es klingelte, …), or work as an attribute to a noun (Relativsatz) — tested with the Ersatzprobe.
evidence: Replace a subordinate clause with a single Satzglied
Classify clauses as Subjekt-, Objekt-, Adverbial- or Attributsatz
Explain why a relative clause is not a Satzglied

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern introduces Subjekt- and Objektsatz in Jgst. 6; NRW in Kl. 7/8.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Infinitive and Participle Phrases
topics.description: Recognise infinitive groups (um … zu, ohne … zu, anstatt … zu) and participle groups (Laut lachend, lief sie davon) as shortened clauses, convert them into full subordinate clauses and back, and use them to write more concisely.
evidence: Turn a damit-clause into an um-zu group
Convert a participle group into a full clause
Use infinitive and participle groups to vary sentence structure
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads 'Vom Regen völlig durchnässt, erreichten wir die Hütte', can they rewrite it as a full clause and say what kind of group it is?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Topological Field Model

Explain how a different Vorfeld changes the emphasis
Use the model to explain verb-final order in subordinate clauses
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares 'Den Schlüssel hat sie vergessen' with 'Sie hat den Schlüssel vergessen', can they show with the field model what changes and why?
topics.laenderNotes: The KMK MSA standards name Satzklammer and Felderstruktur; terminology and depth vary strongly between textbooks.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Cohesive Devices
topics.description: Analyse how texts are held together by cohesive devices — pronouns and other pro-forms, synonyms and repetition (Wiederaufnahme), connectors (deshalb, dennoch, zudem) and articles — and use them deliberately to make own texts coherent.
evidence: Mark the chain of references to a character in a text
Replace repeated nouns with suitable pro-forms
Choose connectors that express the intended logical relation
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} revises an argument, do they link the paragraphs with connectors like 'außerdem' or 'dennoch' and avoid repeating the same noun?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Nominal and Verbal Style
topics.description: Recognise the nominal style typical of official and academic German (Die Durchführung der Untersuchung erfolgt …) as opposed to the verbal style, transform between them and judge their effect: compression and abstraction versus readability.
evidence: Transform nominal constructions into verbal ones and back
Use nominalisations for headings and outlines
Judge when the nominal style hinders understanding
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads 'Nach erfolgter Prüfung der Unterlagen erfolgt die Benachrichtigung', can they rewrite it in plain verbal style?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Denotation and Connotation
topics.description: Distinguish the core meaning of a word (denotation) from its associated, evaluative meanings (connotation), e.g. Hund – Köter – Vierbeiner, and analyse how word choices with positive or negative connotations steer readers.
evidence: Order synonyms by their connotation
Find evaluative word choices in a news text
Rewrite a loaded sentence neutrally
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares 'Flüchtlingswelle' with 'Geflüchtete', can they explain that the meaning overlaps but the connotations differ?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Commas with Infinitive and Participle Groups
topics.description: Apply the comma rules for infinitive groups — obligatory after um, ohne, statt, anstatt, außer, als, or when a noun or pointer word refers to them (Es ist mein Wunsch, …) — and for participle groups, and know where the comma is optional.
evidence: Set the obligatory comma before um … zu and ohne … zu
Recognise pointer words (daran, es) that require a comma
Explain which commas are optional
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes 'Er ging ohne sich umzudrehen', do they add the comma before 'ohne' and explain why it is obligatory?

osMatches.note: German comma rules for infinitive groups have no English equivalent

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Commas with Contrasts and Comparisons
topics.nameDe: Komma bei entgegenstellenden Konjunktionen und Vergleichen (aber, sondern, als, wie)
topics.description: Set a comma before contrasting conjunctions such as aber, sondern, jedoch, doch (klein, aber fein) but not before und/oder in lists, and decide whether als and wie introduce a clause (comma) or only a comparison phrase (no comma: größer als ich).
evidence: Set commas before aber and sondern
Decide on the comma before als/wie by checking for a finite verb
Correct over- and under-use of commas around und
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes 'Sie ist größer, als ich' and 'Er kam nicht heute sondern morgen', can they correct both and explain the rules?

osMatches.note: English comma rules before conjunctions differ

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Writing Words Together or Apart
topics.description: Apply the basic rules of Getrennt- und Zusammenschreibung: verb + verb usually apart (spazieren gehen), separable particle verbs together (zurückgeben), adjective + verb together when a new meaning arises (krankschreiben vs. schnell laufen), and nominalised combinations together and capitalised (beim Spazierengehen).
evidence: Decide between apart and together for common verb combinations
Explain the new-meaning test (schwarzfahren vs. schwarz anmalen)
Write nominalised verb groups correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes 'Wir wollen heute Rad fahren, aber beim radfahren …', can they correct the second to 'beim Radfahren' and explain why?

prerequisites.reason: Nominalised groups are written together and capitalised

osMatches.note: English hyphenation of compounds

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Semicolon, Colon and Dash
topics.description: Use the semicolon between closely related main clauses or between groups in a long list, the colon before explanations, summaries, quotations and lists (capitalising when a full sentence follows), and the dash for pauses, surprises and insertions.
evidence: Replace a full stop with a semicolon between related clauses
Decide between capital and small letter after a colon
Use a dash to set off an insertion or a surprise
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a long list of reasons, do they use semicolons where commas would be confusing and a colon to introduce the list?

prerequisites.reason: Dashes as an alternative to commas

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Spelling Greek and Latin Loanwords
topics.nameDe: Fremdwörter und Fachbegriffe: Schreibung nach Herkunftsmustern
topics.description: Spell loanwords and technical terms by recognising typical Greek, Latin, French and English morphemes and letter patterns — ph, th, rh, y (Philosophie, Theater, Rhythmus, System), -ion, -ieren, -ik, -ell, -eur — and form their plurals correctly (Atlanten, Themen, Praktika).
evidence: Explain the spelling of a technical term by its parts (Bio-logie)
Spell frequent loanword suffixes correctly
Form the plurals of Latin and Greek loanwords
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has to write 'Rhythmus', 'Theorie' and the plural of 'Thema', do they get the rh, th and 'Themen' right and know where these spellings come from?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Latein
externalPrerequisites.concept: Latin word roots and their meaning in loanwords

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Doubtful Cases in Spelling
topics.description: Resolve doubtful cases of German spelling — capitals in fixed phrases (im Allgemeinen, auf Deutsch, recht/Recht haben), multi-word proper names (der Schiefe Turm von Pisa), permitted variants (Fotografie/Photographie) — by consulting the official rules or a dictionary and explaining the decision.
evidence: Look up and explain a doubtful case in the Duden or the official rules
Name cases in which two spellings are permitted
Capitalise multi-word proper names correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is unsure whether to write 'im Allgemeinen' or 'im allgemeinen', do they check a reliable source and explain the rule behind the answer?
topics.laenderNotes: The binding reference is the Amtliches Regelwerk of the Rat für deutsche Rechtschreibung.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Formal Plot Summary
topics.description: Write a formal Inhaltsangabe of a short story or novel chapter: an introductory sentence with author, title, text type, year of publication and theme, then a factual summary of the plot in own words and in the present tense, without quotations or direct speech.
evidence: Write an introductory sentence with all key data and the theme
Summarise the plot in logical order in the Präsens
Replace direct speech with indirect speech or paraphrase
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes an Inhaltsangabe, does it begin with author, title, text type and theme and stay factual, in the present tense, without direct speech?

prerequisites.reason: Summarising plot steps is the first stage
Present tense as the summary tense

osMatches.note: os: précis writing

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Character Analysis Essay
topics.description: Write a characterisation of a literary figure: introduce the character, describe outer features, social situation, behaviour, thoughts and relationships, distinguish direct from indirect characterisation and support each statement with quotations.
evidence: Collect direct and indirect characterisation with line references
Structure the text from outer features to inner traits
Close with an evaluation of the character's development
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} characterises a figure from a novel, do they move from appearance to behaviour and attitudes and back up their claims with quotations?

prerequisites.reason: Claims are supported with text passages

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Descriptive Mood Writing
topics.description: Write a Schilderung that conveys the atmosphere of a place or moment through subjective sensory impressions, vivid adjectives and verbs, images and comparisons, usually in the present tense and without a plot — unlike the objective Beschreibung.
evidence: Collect impressions for all five senses
Use images and comparisons to create a mood
Explain the difference between Schilderung and Beschreibung
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes about a market at dawn, does the reader feel the atmosphere through sounds, smells and images rather than reading a factual list?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Formal Letters and E-Mails
topics.description: Write formal letters and e-mails to institutions or companies (request, complaint, enquiry about a work placement) following DIN 5008 layout: sender, address, date, subject line, formal salutation and closing, a clear concern and a polite, factual tone.
evidence: Lay out a formal letter with all required parts
State the concern clearly in the first paragraph
Use formal salutations and closings and the polite Sie
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes to the town council about a broken playground, does the letter have a subject line, a formal salutation, a clear request and a polite closing?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Linear Argumentative Essay
topics.description: Write an argumentative text on a debatable question that supports one position with several arguments, each developed as claim, reason and example, arranged in increasing order of weight and framed by an introduction and a conclusion.
evidence: Develop each argument with claim, reason and example
Order the arguments from weakest to strongest
Write an introduction leading to the question and a conclusion stating the result
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} argues for a longer lunch break, does each paragraph give a claim, a reason and an example, with the strongest argument last?

prerequisites.reason: The statement of opinion is the first step

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Commentary and Letter to the Editor
topics.description: Write opinion pieces for a newspaper or website: a Leserbrief that responds to an article and a Kommentar that takes a clear position on a current issue, using journalistic conventions such as a catchy headline, a reference to the occasion and a pointed conclusion.
evidence: Refer clearly to the article or event that prompted the text
Take and justify a clear position for a public audience
Use a headline and a pointed final sentence
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} disagrees with a newspaper article about young people and phones, can they write a Leserbrief that refers to the article and argues convincingly?

prerequisites.reason: The Kommentar as a journalistic genre

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Minutes and Notes
topics.description: Take structured notes while listening and write minutes: a Verlaufsprotokoll that records the course of a lesson or meeting and an Ergebnisprotokoll that records only results and decisions, with header data, present tense and reported speech.
evidence: Take notes during a discussion with key words and abbreviations
Write an Ergebnisprotokoll with header and numbered results
Distinguish Verlaufs- and Ergebnisprotokoll
topics.assessmentPrompt: After a class council meeting, can {{name}} write minutes that list date, participants, agenda and the decisions taken?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Quoting and Referencing
topics.description: Quote correctly from texts: mark direct quotations with quotation marks and line or page references (Z. 12; S. 4 f.), integrate quotations grammatically into own sentences, mark omissions and changes with square brackets, paraphrase with a reference and list sources.
evidence: Integrate a quotation grammatically into an own sentence
Mark omissions with […] and give line numbers
Paraphrase a passage and give the source
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} supports a claim in an analysis, do they quote with quotation marks and a line number and fit the quotation smoothly into their sentence?

prerequisites.reason: Readings are supported with text passages

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Writing a Literary Analysis
topics.description: Write an analysis of a literary text: an introduction with key data and a first interpretation hypothesis (Deutungshypothese), a main part that links content, structure and language devices to their function with quotations, and a conclusion that checks the hypothesis.
evidence: Formulate a Deutungshypothese in the introduction
Link each observed device to its effect and meaning
Return to and refine the hypothesis in the conclusion
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} analyses a short story, do they start with an interpretation hypothesis and then show how specific devices support it, with quotations?

prerequisites.reason: An analysis usually begins with a short summary
Interpretations are justified with the text

topics.laenderNotes: NRW Klassenarbeit type 4a (analysieren und interpretieren) from Kl. 7; Bayern asks for first Deutungshypothesen in Jgst. 9.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Creative Interpretation
topics.nameDe: Gestaltendes Interpretieren: Leerstellen füllen und begründen
topics.description: Write a creative text that fills a gap in a literary text — an inner monologue, a diary entry or letter by a character, an additional scene — consistent with the original's characters, situation and language, and explain which interpretation of the original it expresses.
evidence: Write an inner monologue that fits the character and situation
Stay consistent with the facts and style of the original
Explain in a commentary which reading of the text the piece expresses
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes a character's diary entry after a key scene, does it fit what we know about the character and can they explain what it shows about their reading of the story?

prerequisites.reason: The text must fit the character

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Pro and Con Argumentative Essay
topics.description: Write a dialectical Erörterung that weighs arguments for and against a question, arranged in block or alternating structure, uses transitions between the sides and ends with a reasoned judgement or compromise.
evidence: Plan a balanced outline with pro and contra arguments
Use transitions to switch between the sides
Draw a justified conclusion that follows from the weighing
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} discusses whether school should start later, do they weigh both sides fairly and reach a conclusion that follows from their arguments?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Types of Arguments
topics.description: Distinguish types of arguments — fact-based, authority, normative (values), analogy, experience and indirect (refuting the opposite) — judge their persuasiveness and validity and use them deliberately, avoiding sweeping generalisations.
evidence: Classify arguments by type
Judge the strength of an argument and find its weak points
Replace a generalisation with a supported argument
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears 'Alle Experten sagen, dass …', can they recognise an argument from authority and ask how strong it really is?

prerequisites.reason: Arguments are first built in linear essays

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Argumentative Writing from Materials
topics.description: Write an argumentative text (e.g. a commentary or speech) on the basis of a set of materials — articles, statistics, cartoons: evaluate the materials, take arguments and evidence from them with references and develop an own position for a defined audience.
evidence: Evaluate materials for relevance and reliability
Use figures and statements from the materials as evidence with references
Develop an own, clearly marked position
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given four materials on a speed limit, can {{name}} write a commentary that uses evidence from the materials with references and reaches their own position?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Job Application Letter
topics.description: Write an application for a work placement, job or scholarship — as a letter, e-mail or online form: refer to the advertisement, show motivation and suitable skills with examples, and follow the formal conventions of a business letter.
evidence: Refer to the specific advertisement and company
Present motivation and skills with concrete evidence
Follow the layout and tone of a formal letter or e-mail
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} applies for a work placement, does the letter explain why this company, which skills they bring with examples, and follow the formal format?
topics.laenderNotes: Usually taught in Kl. 9 together with the Betriebspraktikum; NRW Kernlehrplan Kl. 9/10.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Curriculum Vitae
topics.description: Write a tabular CV as expected in Germany: personal data, schooling, practical experience, skills and interests in a consistent (usually reverse) chronological order with a clear layout, place and date.
evidence: Order entries consistently in reverse chronological order
Select information that is relevant for the application
Lay out the CV clearly and consistently
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} prepares a CV for a work placement, is it complete, clearly ordered and suited to the placement they apply for?

prerequisites.reason: CV and letter together form the application

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Writing Excerpts
topics.description: Excerpt a non-fiction text for a defined question: extract the relevant statements as key points or short quotations with page references, structure them and keep the source data, as preparation for presentations, essays and later the Facharbeit.
evidence: Formulate a guiding question before excerpting
Extract only relevant information with page numbers
Record the full source data
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} prepares a presentation from a book chapter, do they write an excerpt that answers their question, with page numbers and the source?

prerequisites.reason: The text must be understood first

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Comparing Several Sources
topics.description: Read several texts or web sources on the same topic comparatively: collect what each says on defined aspects in a table (Synopse), note agreements, contradictions and gaps, and draw conclusions about the topic and the reliability of the sources.
evidence: Set up a comparison table with aspects and sources
Mark agreements and contradictions between sources
Draw a justified conclusion from the comparison
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads three articles about the same event, can they show in a table where the articles agree, where they contradict each other and what that means?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Narrative Mode
topics.description: Analyse the narrative mode of a text: an auktorial narrator who knows and comments on everything, a personal narrator bound to one character's perception, or a neutral narrator who only reports what can be observed — and describe the effect on the reader.
evidence: Identify the narrative mode with evidence from the text
Rewrite a passage in a different narrative mode
Explain how the mode steers the reader's sympathy
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads a passage where the narrator knows what every character thinks and comments on it, can they call it auktorial and explain the effect?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on narrator and point of view

topics.laenderNotes: Most schools use Stanzel's terms (auktorial, personal, neutral); some textbooks and Bayern (Jgst. 10: Fokalisierung) switch to Genette-based terms.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Narrative Time
topics.nameDe: Erzählzeit und erzählte Zeit (Zeitraffung, Zeitdehnung, Rückblende)
topics.description: Compare the time it takes to read a passage (Erzählzeit) with the time span of the events (erzählte Zeit), identify time-lapse, scene-like and stretched narration as well as flashbacks and foreshadowing, and explain how the handling of time creates emphasis and suspense.
evidence: Decide whether a passage is zeitraffend, zeitdeckend or zeitdehnend
Find flashbacks and foreshadowing
Explain why an author stretches a key moment
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} notices that a few seconds of an accident fill two pages, can they call it Zeitdehnung and explain why the author does that?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Presenting Speech and Thought
topics.nameDe: Darbietungsformen: Erzählerbericht, Figurenrede, innerer Monolog, erlebte Rede
topics.description: Distinguish how a narrative presents events and consciousness — Erzählerbericht, direct and indirect Figurenrede, innerer Monolog (first person, present tense) and erlebte Rede (third person, past tense, the character's perspective) — and analyse their effect.
evidence: Identify erlebte Rede and innerer Monolog by person and tense
Transform a passage of erlebte Rede into an inner monologue
Explain how the mode creates closeness to a character
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads 'Morgen würde sie es ihm sagen. Ganz bestimmt.', can they identify it as erlebte Rede and explain the effect?

prerequisites.reason: The narrative mode is the frame

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: The Short Story
topics.description: Recognise and interpret the features of the German Kurzgeschichte — abrupt beginning, open ending, everyday situation with a turning point, few characters, everyday language — including its post-war origins (Borchert, Böll, Aichinger) and contemporary examples.
evidence: Identify genre features in a Kurzgeschichte with evidence
Interpret the open ending
Relate a post-war Kurzgeschichte to its historical context
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads Borchert's 'Das Brot', can they show the typical features of a Kurzgeschichte and explain what the open ending leaves to the reader?

prerequisites.reason: Open endings call for own readings

topics.laenderNotes: NRW and Baden-Württemberg place the Kurzgeschichte in Kl. 7/8, Bayern in Jgst. 9; the post-war context is usually added in Kl. 9/10.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: The Ballad
topics.nameDe: Ballade: Erzählgedicht zwischen Lyrik, Epik und Dramatik
topics.description: Understand the ballad as a poem that tells a dramatic story, combining lyric form (verse, rhyme, stanzas), epic narration and dramatic dialogue — classic examples by Goethe (Erlkönig), Schiller (Die Bürgschaft) and Fontane (John Maynard) — and recite and interpret it.
evidence: Show lyric, epic and dramatic elements in a ballad
Summarise and interpret the conflict of a ballad
Recite a ballad expressively
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads Goethe's 'Erlkönig', can they show where the poem rhymes, where it tells a story and where characters speak in dialogue?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Short Narrative Forms
topics.description: Distinguish short traditional narrative forms — the Anekdote with its pointed ending about a real person, the Kalendergeschichte (Hebel, Brecht) with a practical lesson and the humorous Schwank (Till Eulenspiegel) — and explain how each makes its point.
evidence: Assign short texts to Anekdote, Kalendergeschichte or Schwank
Explain the punch line of an Anekdote
Formulate the lesson of a Kalendergeschichte
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads one of Hebel's Kalendergeschichten, can they say what lesson it teaches and how it differs from an Anekdote?
topics.laenderNotes: Baden-Württemberg names Kalendergeschichte and Anekdote for Kl. 7/8; other Länder include them under 'epische Kleinformen'.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: The Novella
topics.description: Recognise the Novelle as a medium-length narrative about an 'unheard-of event' (Goethe) with a clear turning point, often a frame story and a central symbol (Falkentheorie), and interpret a 19th-century Novelle such as Storm's 'Der Schimmelreiter' or Kleist's 'Das Erdbeben in Chili'.
evidence: Identify the unheard-of event and the turning point
Explain the function of frame and inner story
Interpret the central symbol of a Novelle
topics.assessmentPrompt: After reading 'Der Schimmelreiter', can {{name}} explain the frame structure and what the white horse stands for?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern places the Novelle in Jgst. 10; Baden-Württemberg names it from Kl. 7/8; NRW includes it under 'Erzählung' in Kl. 9/10.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: The Parable
topics.description: Interpret parables (Kafka, Brecht, Lessing's Ringparabel) by transferring the concrete image level (Bildebene) to a general meaning level (Sachebene), recognising that modern parables often leave the transfer open.
evidence: Distinguish Bildebene and Sachebene
Transfer the image of a parable to a general statement
Discuss why Kafka's parables resist a single meaning
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads Kafka's 'Gibs auf!', can they explain what the lost man could stand for and why there is more than one possible reading?

prerequisites.reason: Fables also carry a transferable meaning

topics.laenderNotes: Named for Kl. 9/10 in Baden-Württemberg; elsewhere often part of the Aufklärung unit (Ringparabel) or of the Oberstufe.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Analysing a Novel
topics.description: Analyse a whole novel (e.g. a 20th- or 21st-century novel) by tracing plot strands, narrative structure and handling of time, central motifs, the development and constellation of characters, and by relating the work to its historical context.
evidence: Map the plot strands and their connections
Trace a character's development across the novel
Relate a central motif to the novel's theme
topics.assessmentPrompt: After reading a novel in class, can {{name}} explain how its plot strands connect and how a central motif develops the theme?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Analysing a Drama Scene
topics.description: Analyse a scene from a play: place it in the overall plot, divide the dialogue into phases, and describe how the conflict and the relationship between the characters develop and what speech acts and stage directions reveal.
evidence: Place the scene in the course of the play
Divide the dialogue into phases and name the turning point
Describe how power shifts between the characters
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} analyses a quarrel scene, can they show in which phases the dialogue proceeds and who gains the upper hand?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Classical Drama Structure
topics.nameDe: Klassisches Drama: Fünf-Akt-Schema, Tragödie und Komödie
topics.description: Understand the structure of a classical drama — five acts following Freytag's pyramid (exposition, rising action, climax and Peripetie, retarding moment, catastrophe) and the unities of action, time and place — and distinguish tragedy from comedy, working with a whole play (e.g. by Lessing or Schiller).
evidence: Assign the acts of a play to Freytag's pyramid
Name the Peripetie and the retarding moment
Distinguish tragic and comic structure
topics.assessmentPrompt: After reading a classical play, can {{name}} show in which act the turning point happens and why the ending is tragic?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern requires a drama as a whole text in Jgst. 10 (often Lessing's 'Nathan der Weise'); NRW in Kl. 9/10; in many Länder the first complete classical drama is read in the Einführungsphase.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Poetry Analysis
topics.nameDe: Gedichtanalyse: Form, Sprache und Inhalt im Zusammenhang
topics.description: Analyse a poem systematically — speaker and situation, structure, rhyme, metre, cadence (männlich/weiblich) and enjambement, images and sound — and show how form and language support the content and mood.
evidence: Describe formal features including cadence and enjambement
Explain the function of images and sound devices
Link formal observations to an interpretation
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} analyses a nature poem, do they explain how its rhythm and images create the mood rather than just listing devices?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Rhetorical Devices
topics.description: Identify rhetorical devices at word, sentence and thought level — alliteration, anaphora, parallelism, chiasmus, climax, antithesis, ellipsis, hyperbole, irony, euphemism, rhetorical question — and explain their function in literary texts, non-fiction and speeches.
evidence: Name the devices in a passage with correct terms
Explain the function of a device in context
Use selected devices in own speeches or commentaries
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads a speech full of repeated sentence openings and contrasts, can they name the devices and say what effect they create?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Motif and Symbol
topics.nameDe: Motiv und Symbol in literarischen Texten
topics.description: Recognise recurring motifs (e.g. the wanderer, the window, the journey) and symbols (an object standing for an abstract idea) in literature, distinguish them from simple metaphors and use them to interpret a text and to compare texts with related motifs.
evidence: Trace a recurring motif through a text
Explain what a symbol stands for in context
Compare how two texts use the same motif
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} notices that a window appears in several key scenes, can they explain it as a motif and say what it means for the story?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Comparing Literary Texts
topics.description: Compare two literary texts (e.g. poems on the same motif or two short stories) by defined aspects — theme, form, language, perspective, context — work out similarities and differences and explain them.
evidence: Choose or apply comparison aspects
Present similarities and differences in a structured way
Explain differences with reference to context or intention
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares two city poems, do they compare them aspect by aspect and explain why they view the city so differently?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Text and Historical Context
topics.nameDe: Texte im Kontext deuten (Entstehungszeit, Biografie, Epoche)
topics.description: Use information about a text's time of origin, the author's life and the literary period to deepen an interpretation, while distinguishing evidence from the text from contextual knowledge and not simply equating author and narrator.
evidence: Research relevant context information for a text
Explain how context changes the understanding of a passage
Separate text evidence from context in an argument
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} interprets a post-war short story, do they use the historical situation to explain details while still arguing from the text?

prerequisites.reason: Post-war short stories as a typical case

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Film Analysis
topics.description: Analyse film scenes with film terms — camera movement, montage and cut (shot/reverse shot, parallel montage), lighting, sound and music — and explain how they tell the story, create suspense and shape the viewer's view of characters.
evidence: Describe a sequence using shot, angle, camera movement and cut
Explain the effect of montage and music
Write a short sequence protocol
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a chase scene, can they explain how quick cuts and music create tension?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Journalistic Text Types
topics.nameDe: Journalistische Textsorten: Nachricht, Bericht, Reportage, Kommentar, Glosse
topics.description: Distinguish informing journalistic forms (Meldung, Nachricht built as an inverted pyramid, Bericht, Reportage, Interview) from opinion forms (Kommentar, Glosse, Leitartikel, Rezension), in print and online, and describe their structure and intention.
evidence: Classify newspaper texts by text type
Describe the inverted-pyramid structure of a news report
Explain the different intentions of Reportage and Kommentar
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is given a news report and a commentary on the same event, can they tell which is which and show the differences?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Analysing Advertisements
topics.nameDe: Werbung analysieren: sprachliche und bildliche Mittel
topics.description: Analyse adverts in print, video and social media: the AIDA model, slogans, wordplay and imperatives, image composition, the target group and the role models presented, and evaluate how the advert tries to influence.
evidence: Apply the AIDA model to an advert
Analyse slogan language (wordplay, comparison, imperative)
Describe the target group and the role images shown
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at an influencer advert for sneakers, can they explain which language and image techniques are used and who is targeted?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Analysing Non-Fiction Texts
topics.description: Analyse a non-fiction or argumentative text (e.g. commentary, essay, speech): state topic and thesis, trace the line of argument, identify argument types and language devices, and explain how they serve the author's intention for the target audience.
evidence: Reconstruct the line of argument paragraph by paragraph
Identify the author's intention and target audience
Explain how language devices support the intention
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} analyses a newspaper commentary, can they show step by step how the author argues and which language devices are used to persuade?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Media Constructions and Disinformation
topics.nameDe: Mediale Darstellungen als Konstrukt: Desinformation und Meinungsbildung
topics.description: Understand media representations as constructed: analyse how framing, selection, image manipulation and algorithmic personalisation shape what is shown, how fake news is built to spread, and how claims can be checked (lateral reading, fact-checking sites).
evidence: Analyse how a post or article frames an event
Check a viral claim by lateral reading
Explain how personalised feeds narrow the information spectrum
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a shocking viral post, do they check who is behind it and whether reliable sources confirm it before sharing?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Visualising a Presentation
topics.description: Design visual support for presentations — slides with few key words and meaningful images, diagrams and structure charts, a one-page handout — following design rules (contrast, font size, one idea per slide) and coordinating speech and visuals.
evidence: Design slides with key words instead of full sentences
Turn information into a diagram or structure chart
Create a handout that summarises the talk
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} prepares slides, do they use few words and clear images and talk freely instead of reading from the screen?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Writing and Giving a Speech
topics.description: Write and deliver a persuasive speech for an occasion (e.g. a school assembly or student council election): adapt it to audience and occasion, structure it with an attention-grabbing opening and a memorable close, use rhetorical devices and control voice and body language.
evidence: Structure a speech with opening, argument and appeal
Use at least three rhetorical devices purposefully
Deliver the speech freely with eye contact and pauses
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gives a speech for the student council election, does it grab attention at the start, argue convincingly and end with a clear appeal?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Formal Debate
topics.description: Take part in a formal debate on a question that requires a decision (Soll …?): timed opening statements, a free exchange responding to opponents, closing statements, and judge debaters by criteria such as subject knowledge, expressiveness, conversational skill and persuasiveness.
evidence: Give a timed opening statement with a clear position
Respond directly to an opponent's argument
Judge a debate by agreed criteria
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a class debate on 'Soll das Wahlalter auf 16 gesenkt werden?', does {{name}} respond to what the other side said and close with a well-reasoned position?
topics.laenderNotes: The 'Jugend debattiert' format (opening round, free exchange, closing round) is used in many Gymnasien from Kl. 8.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Job Interview
topics.description: Prepare and practise interviews for a job or work placement in role play: research the company, answer typical questions about motivation and strengths, ask own questions, and use an appropriate register, body language and politeness.
evidence: Prepare answers to typical interview questions
Ask informed questions about the company
Reflect on own body language in a recorded role play
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a mock interview for a work placement, can {{name}} explain convincingly why they want this placement and ask a sensible question themselves?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Interpreting Through Drama Methods
topics.description: Use drama methods to interpret literary texts: write a role biography, build freeze frames of character constellations, speak as a character's inner voice (Hilfs-Ich) or stage a scene in different ways, and reflect on what each version reveals about the text.
evidence: Build a freeze frame of a character constellation and explain it
Speak as a character's inner voice in a key scene
Compare two stagings of a scene and the interpretations behind them
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s group builds a freeze frame of a drama scene, can they explain how distance and posture show the relationships between the characters?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Youth Language
topics.description: Examine youth language as a variety of German: typical features (new words, borrowings from English and other languages, shortened forms, intensifiers), its functions (group identity, demarcation, creativity) and when it is appropriate compared with standard language.
evidence: Collect and classify features of current youth language
Explain the social functions of youth language
Translate between youth language and standard language and judge appropriateness
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears 'Das ist lowkey cringe', can they explain what makes it youth language and when they would not use it?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Four-Sides Communication Model
topics.nameDe: Kommunikationsquadrat (Schulz von Thun): Sach- und Beziehungsebene
topics.description: Analyse everyday conversations with Schulz von Thun's four-sides model: every message has a factual content, a self-revelation, a relationship side and an appeal, and misunderstandings arise when sender and receiver focus on different sides.
evidence: Analyse a message on all four sides
Explain a misunderstanding by different 'ears'
Rephrase a message to avoid a relationship conflict
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a passenger says 'Die Ampel ist grün' to a driver, can {{name}} explain the four messages the driver might hear?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Stages of German and Meaning Change
topics.description: Know the historical stages of German (Althochdeutsch, Mittelhochdeutsch, Frühneuhochdeutsch, Neuhochdeutsch), read short Middle High German passages with help, and describe kinds of meaning change — broadening, narrowing, improvement and deterioration (e.g. Weib, geil, hôchgezît).
evidence: Order the stages of German on a timeline
Translate a short Middle High German passage with a glossary
Classify examples of meaning change
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learns that 'hôchgezît' once meant any festival, can they explain which kind of meaning change led to today's 'Hochzeit'?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Discriminatory and Inclusive Language
topics.description: Analyse how language can stereotype and discriminate (clichés, labels, the generic masculine) and compare forms of gender-fair language in German (pair forms, neutral forms, gender symbols), discussing arguments in the public debate and the position of the Rat für deutsche Rechtschreibung.
evidence: Identify discriminating wording and clichés in texts
Rewrite a text with different gender-fair forms
Discuss arguments for and against gender symbols
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads 'Jeder Schüler muss seinen Ausweis zeigen', can they name several ways to phrase it gender-fairly and discuss their pros and cons?
topics.laenderNotes: Some Länder (e.g. Bayern, Hessen, Sachsen) do not allow gender symbols such as * or : in official school writing; teaching the debate is common everywhere.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Manipulative Language
topics.description: Recognise linguistic means of manipulation in advertising, politics and social media — loaded words, euphemisms, suggestive questions, false alternatives, generalisations, repetition, emotional images — and distinguish legitimate persuasion from manipulation.
evidence: Find manipulative techniques in a text or post
Rewrite a manipulative statement neutrally
Explain the difference between persuading and manipulating
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads a post asking 'Wollen wir wirklich zusehen, wie unsere Stadt zerstört wird?', can they identify the suggestive question and loaded words?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Language of Closeness and Distance
topics.nameDe: Konzeptionelle und mediale Mündlichkeit und Schriftlichkeit
topics.description: Distinguish the medium (spoken vs. written) from the conception of language (language of closeness vs. language of distance, after Koch and Oesterreicher): a chat is written but conceptually oral, a lecture spoken but conceptually written — and judge which conception suits a situation.
evidence: Place text types on the closeness–distance continuum
Identify oral features in a written chat
Turn a chat message into a conceptually written e-mail
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares a messenger message with a formal e-mail, can they explain why both are written but only one is conceptually written?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: The Enlightenment in Literature
topics.description: Understand the Enlightenment (c. 1720–1785) as the first literary period studied in depth: the ideals of reason, tolerance and autonomy (Kant's 'Sapere aude'), fable and drama as means of education, and works by Lessing such as 'Nathan der Weise' (Ringparabel) or 'Emilia Galotti'.
evidence: Explain key ideas of the Enlightenment with Kant's definition
Interpret the Ringparabel as a plea for tolerance
Show Enlightenment ideas in a literary text
topics.assessmentPrompt: After reading 'Nathan der Weise', can {{name}} explain what the Ringparabel says about religion and why this is typical of the Enlightenment?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: Enlightenment and absolutism in the 18th century

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern places the Aufklärung in Jgst. 10, Niedersachsen and most NRW school curricula in the Einführungsphase (Kl. 11), Baden-Württemberg in Kl. 9/10 (2016 plan, G8). In G8 Länder such as Sachsen or Thüringen it falls about one year earlier.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Literary Periods as Constructs
topics.description: Use literary periods (Epochen) from the Baroque to the present as an orientation framework, know their sequence and approximate dates, and reflect that period labels are later constructs with overlaps, parallel currents and exceptions.
evidence: Order the main literary periods with approximate dates
Explain why period boundaries are disputed
Name works that fit two periods or none
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} place Sturm und Drang, Klassik and Romantik on a timeline and explain why Goethe does not fit neatly into one period?

prerequisites.reason: The first period studied in depth

topics.laenderNotes: Baden-Württemberg asks for reflection on period models from Kl. 9/10; Bayern does so in Jgst. 11 with Barock, Aufklärung and Sturm und Drang.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Baroque Poetry
topics.nameDe: Barock: Vanitas, Memento mori und Carpe diem
topics.description: Interpret Baroque poetry of the 17th century against the background of the Thirty Years' War: the themes of vanitas, memento mori and carpe diem, the antithetical style and the sonnet form, e.g. Andreas Gryphius' 'Es ist alles eitel' or 'Tränen des Vaterlandes'.
evidence: Explain vanitas, memento mori and carpe diem
Analyse the antithetical structure of a Baroque sonnet
Relate a poem to the experience of the Thirty Years' War
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads Gryphius' 'Es ist alles eitel', can they explain the vanitas idea and how the antitheses express it?
topics.laenderNotes: Optional in many Länder; Bayern (Jgst. 11) and Baden-Württemberg include it; the KMK standards refer to the Baroque as background for comparing motifs.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Storm and Stress
topics.nameDe: Sturm und Drang: Genie, Gefühl und Rebellion
topics.description: Understand the Sturm und Drang (c. 1765–1785) as a youthful revolt against the rationalism of the Enlightenment and against social constraints: the cult of the genius, feeling and nature and the rebellion against authority, in works such as Goethe's 'Prometheus' and 'Die Leiden des jungen Werthers' or Schiller's 'Die Räuber'.
evidence: Explain the ideals of genius, feeling and nature
Interpret 'Prometheus' as a poem of revolt
Compare Sturm und Drang ideas with the Enlightenment
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads Goethe's 'Prometheus', can they explain whom the speaker rebels against and why that is typical of the Sturm und Drang?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Weimar Classicism
topics.description: Understand Weimar Classicism (c. 1786–1805) around Goethe and Schiller: the ideal of humanity, the harmony of reason and feeling, the orientation to antiquity and aesthetic education, in works such as Goethe's 'Iphigenie auf Tauris' and 'Faust I' or Schiller's ballads and dramas.
evidence: Explain the ideal of humanity using a key text
Show the classical ideal of form in a drama or poem
Distinguish Klassik from Sturm und Drang
topics.assessmentPrompt: After reading 'Iphigenie auf Tauris', can {{name}} explain how Iphigenie's truthfulness reflects the humanity ideal of the Klassik?

prerequisites.reason: The Klassik follows and tames the Sturm und Drang

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: the French Revolution of 1789 and its reception in Germany

topics.laenderNotes: Goethe's 'Faust I' is a frequent set text for the Zentralabitur; the lists of obligatory texts differ by Land and change every few years.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Romanticism
topics.description: Understand German Romanticism (c. 1795–1835): longing (the blue flower), night, nature and the unconscious, the turn to the Middle Ages and folk poetry, Romantic irony and the idea of a 'progressive Universalpoesie', with texts by Novalis, Eichendorff, E. T. A. Hoffmann and the Brothers Grimm.
evidence: Explain central Romantic motifs with examples
Interpret an Eichendorff poem as typically Romantic
Compare Romantic and Enlightenment views of reason
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads Eichendorff's 'Mondnacht', can they show which Romantic motifs appear and what longing the poem expresses?

prerequisites.reason: Contemporary to and contrasting with the Klassik

externalPrerequisites.subject: Musik
externalPrerequisites.concept: the Romantic art song (Lied) and settings of poems
externalPrerequisites.reason: Many Romantic poems are known as songs

topics.laenderNotes: Niedersachsen's compulsory module asks 'Romantik als Gegenbewegung zur Aufklärung?'.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Vormärz and Political Literature
topics.nameDe: Vormärz und Junges Deutschland: politische Literatur
topics.description: Understand the Vormärz (c. 1830–1848) as a politically engaged literature against censorship and restoration: political poetry and satire (Heine, Herwegh), Büchner's 'Der Hessische Landbote' and 'Woyzeck', and the debate about the writer's role in society.
evidence: Explain the political situation and censorship after 1815
Analyse a political poem by Heine
Explain Büchner's social criticism in 'Woyzeck' or the 'Landbote'
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads Heine's 'Die schlesischen Weber', can they explain its political message and connect it to the Vormärz?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: Restoration, Vormärz and the revolution of 1848/49

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Poetic Realism
topics.description: Understand Poetic Realism (c. 1848–1890) as a depiction of everyday bourgeois reality transfigured by art ('Verklärung'), with the Novelle and the novel as typical genres and authors such as Fontane ('Effi Briest'), Storm and Keller.
evidence: Explain the realist programme of 'Verklärung'
Analyse the depiction of society in a realist novel or Novelle
Distinguish Realismus from Naturalismus
topics.assessmentPrompt: After reading 'Effi Briest', can {{name}} explain how Fontane shows the pressure of social conventions without open protest?

prerequisites.reason: The Novelle is a typical realist genre

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Naturalism
topics.description: Understand Naturalism (c. 1880–1900) as an attempt to depict reality scientifically: determination by milieu and heredity, the social question of industrialisation, the Sekundenstil and dialect, in works such as Gerhart Hauptmann's 'Die Weber' or 'Bahnwärter Thiel'.
evidence: Explain Arno Holz's formula Kunst = Natur – x
Show milieu determination in a naturalist text
Identify the Sekundenstil and its effect
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads 'Bahnwärter Thiel', can they explain how environment and inner drives determine Thiel's fate?

prerequisites.reason: The Sekundenstil is a technique of time

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: industrialisation and the social question in the German Empire

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Literature Around 1900
topics.nameDe: Literatur um 1900: Moderne, Ästhetizismus und Sprachkrise
topics.description: Understand the plural currents of the early Moderne around 1900 — Impressionism, Symbolism, Décadence, Jugendstil — and their shared experience of crisis: the loss of a unified self, the Sprachkrise (Hofmannsthal's 'Chandos-Brief') and new narrative forms such as Schnitzler's interior monologue.
evidence: Name currents of the Moderne around 1900 and their features
Explain the Sprachkrise using the Chandos-Brief
Analyse the interior monologue in Schnitzler's 'Leutnant Gustl' or 'Fräulein Else'
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads an excerpt from the Chandos-Brief, can they explain why the writer feels he can no longer trust words?
