topics.laenderNotes: Niedersachsen: compulsory module 'Krise und Erneuerung des Erzählens' (Literatur um 1900).

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Expressionism
topics.description: Interpret Expressionist poetry and prose (c. 1910–1925): the city as threat, the dissolution of the self, apocalyptic visions and war, the Reihungsstil and drastic imagery, e.g. Jakob van Hoddis' 'Weltende', Georg Heym, Gottfried Benn, Else Lasker-Schüler or Georg Trakl.
evidence: Explain typical Expressionist themes
Analyse the Reihungsstil and imagery in 'Weltende'
Compare an Expressionist city poem with an earlier one
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads 'Weltende', can they explain how the list of unconnected images creates a sense of catastrophe?

prerequisites.reason: Continues the crisis of the Moderne

externalPrerequisites.subject: Kunst
externalPrerequisites.concept: Expressionist painting (Die Brücke, Der Blaue Reiter)
externalPrerequisites.reason: Parallel movement in the visual arts

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Literature of the Weimar Republic
topics.nameDe: Literatur der Weimarer Republik und Neue Sachlichkeit
topics.description: Understand the literature of the Weimar Republic (1918–1933): the Neue Sachlichkeit with its sober, reportage-like style and Gebrauchslyrik (Kästner), the big-city novel (Döblin's 'Berlin Alexanderplatz', Keun's 'Das kunstseidene Mädchen') and the montage technique.
evidence: Explain the style of the Neue Sachlichkeit
Analyse montage in a passage of 'Berlin Alexanderplatz'
Relate a text to the social situation of the Weimar Republic
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads a poem by Kästner, can they explain what is 'sachlich' about its tone and what it criticises?

prerequisites.reason: The Neue Sachlichkeit reacts to Expressionism

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Exile Literature
topics.description: Understand the literature of authors who fled National Socialism (Brecht, Thomas Mann, Anna Seghers, Mascha Kaléko, Klaus Mann): experiences of exile, loss of language and home, resistance and warning, e.g. in Seghers' 'Transit' or Brecht's exile poems.
evidence: Explain why and where German authors went into exile
Analyse the experience of exile in a poem or novel excerpt
Relate exile literature to the book burnings and censorship of 1933
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads Brecht's 'Gedanken über die Dauer des Exils', can they explain the speaker's situation and hopes?

prerequisites.reason: Follows the end of the Weimar Republic

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: the National Socialist dictatorship and persecution 1933–1945
externalPrerequisites.reason: Exile is a consequence of Nazi persecution

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Post-War Literature
topics.description: Understand German literature after 1945: the 'Kahlschlag' and Trümmerliteratur with reduced language (Eich's 'Inventur', Borchert), the Gruppe 47, coming to terms with the Nazi past (Böll, Celan's 'Todesfuge') and Adorno's question about poetry after Auschwitz.
evidence: Explain the idea of the Kahlschlag using 'Inventur'
Interpret 'Todesfuge' in its historical context
Name aims of the Gruppe 47
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads Eich's 'Inventur', can they explain why the speaker only lists his few possessions and what that says about 1945?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Literature in Divided Germany
topics.nameDe: Literatur in BRD und DDR (1949–1990) und Wendeliteratur
topics.description: Compare literature in the two German states — socialist realism and its critics in the GDR (Christa Wolf, Wolf Biermann, Reiner Kunze), engaged and later postmodern literature in the Federal Republic — and literature about the fall of the Wall and reunification (Wendeliteratur).
evidence: Explain the conditions of writing under GDR censorship
Analyse a critical GDR text such as a poem by Kunze or Biermann
Describe how the Wende is reflected in a literary text
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads a poem by Reiner Kunze, can they explain how it criticises the GDR and why it was risky to publish?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: the division of Germany and the GDR 1949–1990

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Contemporary Literature
topics.description: Explore trends in contemporary German-language literature: pop literature, intercultural and migrant literature (Saša Stanišić, Emine Sevgi Özdamar), autofiction, literature about climate and digital life, and new forms such as poetry slam and digital literature.
evidence: Name and illustrate three current trends
Analyse a contemporary text with suitable categories
Compare a contemporary text with a traditional treatment of the same theme
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads an excerpt from Stanišić's 'Herkunft', can they explain how it deals with identity and migration and why it is typical of current literature?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Literary Value and the Canon
topics.description: Reflect on how literary value is attributed — by criteria such as aesthetic quality, innovation, relevance and reception history — and on how and why a canon of 'classics' forms, changes and is contested, e.g. from gender or postcolonial perspectives.
evidence: Justify a literary judgement with explicit criteria
Explain how a work entered or left the school canon
Discuss arguments for and against a fixed canon
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a book counts as a 'classic' and argue whether a contemporary novel should be added to the school canon?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Narratology for Prose Analysis
topics.description: Analyse narrative texts with a systematic set of narratological categories — narrator (inside or outside the story), focalisation, distance, order, duration and frequency, reliability — and use the findings as evidence for an interpretation of a novel or Novelle.
evidence: Describe narrator and focalisation of a passage precisely
Identify an unreliable narrator with evidence
Use narratological findings to support an interpretation
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} interprets a novel passage, can they describe precisely who narrates, through whose eyes, and how this supports their reading?

prerequisites.reason: Modes of presenting speech and thought

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Comparative Poetry Interpretation
topics.description: Interpret two poems on the same motif from different periods (e.g. love, nature or city poems), comparing speaker, form, imagery and worldview, and explain the differences with the respective period and its poetics.
evidence: Interpret each poem against its period background
Compare the poems along explicit aspects
Explain differences by the change of period and worldview
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares a Romantic and an Expressionist poem on night or the city, can they explain the differences in view of the two periods?
topics.laenderNotes: Niedersachsen reads motif-related poems from several periods already in the Einführungsphase; NRW sets the vergleichende Interpretation as an Abitur task type.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Closed and Open Drama
topics.nameDe: Geschlossene und offene Form des Dramas
topics.description: Distinguish the closed form of drama (unity of action, time and place, causal plot, elevated language, few characters) from the open form (loose sequence of scenes, many places, a social range of characters, everyday language), comparing e.g. Schiller's 'Kabale und Liebe' with Büchner's 'Woyzeck'.
evidence: List the features of closed and open form
Classify a play with evidence
Explain how the form expresses the play's view of humans and society
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why 'Woyzeck' with its fragmentary scenes counts as an open drama and what this form says about Woyzeck's world?

prerequisites.reason: The closed form is the classical model

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Bourgeois Tragedy
topics.description: Understand the bürgerliches Trauerspiel as a new 18th-century genre that breaks the Ständeklausel by making middle-class characters tragic heroes, and analyse its typical conflict between bourgeois morality, family and aristocratic power in Lessing's 'Emilia Galotti' or Schiller's 'Kabale und Liebe'.
evidence: Explain the Ständeklausel and how the genre breaks it
Analyse the father–daughter and class conflict
Relate the tragedy to Enlightenment ideas
topics.assessmentPrompt: After reading 'Kabale und Liebe', can {{name}} explain why the lovers fail and what that says about the society of the time?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Brecht's Epic Theatre
topics.description: Understand Brecht's epic theatre as a counter-model to Aristotelian drama: instead of empathy and catharsis, the Verfremdungseffekt (songs, direct address, projections, narrator figures) should make the audience think critically about changeable social conditions, e.g. in 'Der gute Mensch von Sezuan' or 'Mutter Courage und ihre Kinder'.
evidence: Contrast Aristotelian and epic theatre
Identify Verfremdungseffekte in a scene
Explain the intended effect on the audience
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a scene where an actor steps out of the role and sings to the audience, can they explain it as a Verfremdungseffekt and say what it is for?

prerequisites.reason: Brecht's development in the Weimar years

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Poetics and Drama Theory
topics.nameDe: Poetologische Konzepte: Aristoteles, Lessing, Schiller, Brecht
topics.description: Relate literary works to poetological programmes — Aristotle's catharsis, Lessing's drama of compassion (Mitleidsdramaturgie), Schiller's theatre as a moral institution, Brecht's epic theatre, Romantic and naturalist programmes — and use them to explain the aesthetic quality of texts.
evidence: Summarise the core of two poetological concepts
Apply a concept to explain how a drama is designed
Compare how two programmes define the effect of art
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Lessing's idea of Mitleid shapes 'Emilia Galotti' and how Brecht would criticise it?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Ambiguity and Multiple Readings
topics.description: Show that ambiguity is a constitutive feature of literary texts, develop and test competing readings (Lesarten) of a passage, and justify which reading is most plausible on the basis of textual evidence.
evidence: Formulate two different readings of an ambiguous passage
Weigh the textual evidence for each reading
Explain why literary texts allow several readings
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads an open text by Kafka, can they develop two different readings and argue which one the text supports better?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Approaches to Interpretation
topics.nameDe: Literaturtheoretische Zugänge: werkimmanent, biografisch, historisch, rezeptionsästhetisch
topics.description: Distinguish basic approaches of literary theory — text-immanent, biographical, historical-sociological, psychoanalytical, reception-aesthetic and gender-oriented — and apply at least two of them to the same text to see what each reveals.
evidence: Describe the focus of four approaches
Apply two approaches to the same text
Reflect on the limits of an approach
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} interpret a short story once text-immanently and once biographically, and explain what each reading shows and misses?
topics.laenderNotes: The KMK standards name literary-theory approaches for all courses; Leistungskurse work with them in more depth and with secondary literature.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Using Secondary Literature
topics.description: Include scholarly secondary texts, philosophical writings and historical documents in the interpretation of a literary work: summarise the critic's thesis, relate it to own findings and take a reasoned position.
evidence: Summarise the thesis of a scholarly interpretation
Confirm or challenge it with own textual evidence
Integrate secondary sources with correct references
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads a scholar's interpretation of 'Faust', can they test it against the text and say where they agree or disagree?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Intertextuality and Motif History
topics.description: Trace how literary works take up, transform and comment on earlier texts, materials and motifs — e.g. the Faust material, the Medea or Prometheus myth, the Doppelgänger motif — from antiquity to the present, and explain what the reworking adds.
evidence: Identify references to an earlier text or myth
Compare two treatments of the same material
Explain the meaning of a modern rewriting
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares Goethe's 'Prometheus' with the Greek myth, can they explain how Goethe changes the material and why?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Latein
externalPrerequisites.reason: Many motifs come from Latin literature

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Film Adaptations as Interpretations
topics.description: Analyse a film adaptation of a literary work as an interpretation: compare plot, characters and focus with the original, explain changes through film-specific means and the director's intention, and judge the adaptation by reasoned criteria.
evidence: Compare a key scene in book and film
Explain changes with film-specific means
Judge the adaptation with explicit criteria
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a film version of a novel changes a key scene and what interpretation of the book this reveals?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Analysing a Stage Production
topics.description: Analyse a theatre production (live or recorded) of a play studied in class — stage design, costumes, acting, cuts and updating (Regietheater) — and explain and judge it as one interpretation of the dramatic text.
evidence: Describe the staging choices of a production
Relate staging choices to the text
Judge whether the production's interpretation convinces
topics.assessmentPrompt: After watching a modern production of 'Faust', can {{name}} explain why the director set it in the present and whether that works?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Film Criticism and Theory
topics.description: Engage with film criticism and basic film theory — e.g. auteur theory, genre theory, film as art or entertainment, the relation of image and reality — and write or evaluate a film review in the light of these positions.
evidence: Analyse the criteria used in a professional film review
Explain one position of film theory
Write a reasoned film review
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} read a professional film review, identify its criteria and write their own review that uses similar arguments?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Theory-Based Argument Analysis
topics.description: Analyse the structure of argumentative texts with a theoretical model such as Toulmin's scheme (claim, data, warrant, backing, rebuttal), reconstruct implicit premises and judge the validity of an argument and its fallacies.
evidence: Reconstruct an argument with the Toulmin scheme
Make an implicit premise explicit
Identify a fallacy and explain it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads an op-ed, can they reconstruct its main argument as claim, data and warrant and show a hidden premise?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Participation in the Digital Public
topics.nameDe: Digitale Öffentlichkeit: Informieren, Teilen und Kommentieren
topics.description: Analyse how information is presented and spread in digital media, check its validity claims, and reflect on the responsibility that comes with generating, sharing and commenting on content — including hate speech, echo chambers and AI-generated texts.
evidence: Check the validity claim of a shared piece of information
Analyse the language of a comment thread
Formulate rules for responsible participation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} analyse a heated comment thread and explain how individual comments shape public opinion?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Media Change and Media Theory
topics.description: Reflect on media change (print, television, internet, AI-generated content) with positions of media theory — e.g. McLuhan's 'the medium is the message', Postman's critique of entertainment, theories of the digital public sphere — and assess their explanatory power today.
evidence: Summarise two positions of media theory
Apply a position to a current media phenomenon
Evaluate how relevant the position is today
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Postman's thesis about entertainment and judge whether it applies to short-video platforms?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW Leistungskurs 'Medientheorie: mediale Umbrüche'; Niedersachsen compulsory module 'Medien im Wandel' with depth by course level.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Multimodal and Serial Storytelling
topics.nameDe: Multimodales Erzählen: Serie, Graphic Novel, Computerspiel
topics.description: Analyse narratives that combine text, image and sound — TV series, graphic novels, video games, audio plays — with categories of narrative analysis (characters, plot, perspective) and media-specific aesthetics.
evidence: Apply narrative categories to a graphic novel or series episode
Explain the interplay of text and image
Compare a multimodal narrative with a printed one
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} analyses a page of a graphic novel, can they explain how panel layout and text create perspective and time?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Interpretation Essay (Abitur)
topics.description: Write a complete interpretation of a literary text or excerpt under exam conditions: develop an interpretation thesis, analyse content, structure and language in their interplay, include genre and period knowledge as the task requires, and reach a well-founded overall interpretation.
evidence: Develop and justify an interpretation thesis
Link analysis findings to an overall interpretation with quotations
Integrate period or genre knowledge where the task requires it
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} interprets a poem in an exam, does the essay move from a thesis via analysis with quotations to a well-founded overall reading?
topics.laenderNotes: Most Länder set obligatory texts or focus topics for the Zentralabitur that change every few years (e.g. Baden-Württemberg's 'Sternchenthemen', NRW's and Niedersachsen's Vorgaben); they are not separate topics here.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Non-Fiction Analysis (Abitur)
topics.description: Analyse a complex non-fiction text (essay, speech, commentary, scholarly text) in exam form: reconstruct the line of argument, determine intention and communicative situation, analyse argumentative and stylistic means and their effect, possibly in comparison with a second text.
evidence: Reconstruct the argument structure of a complex text
Relate the devices to intention and audience
Compare two texts on the same topic methodically
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} analyses a political essay in an exam, can they show how the argument unfolds and how the language serves the author's intention?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Text-Based Argumentative Essay
topics.description: Write a text-based Erörterung: reproduce the thesis and arguments of a non-fiction text, then discuss them critically — agreeing, refuting or modifying with own arguments and examples — and develop a reasoned position on the issue.
evidence: Summarise the author's position accurately
Assess the author's arguments one by one
Develop an own position with additional arguments
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets a commentary on school uniforms, can they first present its argument fairly and then discuss it critically with their own arguments?
topics.laenderNotes: Baden-Württemberg introduces the textgebundene Erörterung in Kl. 9/10; Niedersachsen makes it an obligatory test form in the Einführungsphase.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Argumentative Essay on Literature
topics.description: Discuss a thesis or question about a literary work (e.g. whether a character is responsible for the tragic outcome): analyse relevant passages, weigh interpretations and arguments drawn from text and context, and reach a reasoned judgement.
evidence: Clarify the thesis and its implications
Support arguments with analysis of text passages
Weigh alternative interpretations and conclude
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked whether a character is more victim or perpetrator, can they argue both sides with evidence from the play and reach a judgement?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Material-Based Informative Writing (Abitur)
topics.description: Write an informative text for a defined purpose and audience (e.g. an encyclopedia article or a feature for a website) from a dossier of texts, graphics and data: select and synthesise the relevant information, structure it independently and present it in a suitable form with sources.
evidence: Select the relevant information from a dossier for a given purpose
Synthesise the information in a self-chosen structure
Adapt register and form to the target text type and audience
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given a dossier on language change, can {{name}} write a coherent encyclopedia article that synthesises the materials in their own structure?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Material-Based Argumentative Writing (Abitur)
topics.description: Write an argumentative text (commentary, essay, speech) for a given communicative situation on the basis of a dossier of materials: evaluate the materials critically, use them selectively as evidence and develop an independent, well-structured argument.
evidence: Evaluate the materials for reliability and perspective
Integrate evidence from the materials with references
Develop an independent position suited to the target text type
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given a dossier on AI in school, can {{name}} write a newspaper commentary that uses the materials selectively and argues independently?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Writing an Essay
topics.description: Write an essay as an open, reflective form of argument: approach a question from several angles in a personal, associative but thoughtful way, use examples, quotations and stylistic devices, and favour reflection over a closed result.
evidence: Explore a question from several perspectives
Use examples, anecdotes and quotations reflectively
Distinguish the essay from the Erörterung in structure and style
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes an essay on 'Was ist Heimat?', does it explore the question from different angles in a personal style rather than just listing pros and cons?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern and Baden-Württemberg introduce essayistic writing already in Kl. 10.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Writing a Review
topics.description: Write a review of a book, film or theatre production for a public audience: inform briefly about content and context, analyse selected aspects and give a reasoned evaluation by explicit criteria in an engaging journalistic style.
evidence: Balance information, analysis and evaluation
Justify the evaluation with explicit criteria
Write for a non-specialist audience
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reviews a novel for the school website, do readers learn enough to decide whether to read it, with a reasoned judgement?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Formulating a Research Question
topics.description: Turn a topic into a focused research question, justify the aspects to be examined, plan the investigation and search for literature systematically in library catalogues and academic databases, evaluating sources for scholarly quality.
evidence: Narrow a broad topic into a researchable question
Search a library catalogue and a database with suitable terms
Judge whether a source is scholarly
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to write about Kafka, can they narrow it to a concrete question and find two scholarly sources on it?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Writing a Research Paper
topics.description: Write an academic-style paper (Facharbeit, Seminararbeit) of roughly 10–20 pages: introduction with question and method, a structured main part, a conclusion that answers the question, consistent citations, bibliography and formal layout, and document the work process.
evidence: Structure the paper with a numbered outline and table of contents
Cite and reference sources consistently in one citation style
Answer the research question in the conclusion
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} hand in a Facharbeit whose conclusion clearly answers the question raised in the introduction, with consistent citations and bibliography?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW: Facharbeit in Q1, replacing a Klausur; Bayern: Seminararbeit in the W-Seminar; other Länder use a project paper or Besondere Lernleistung; it can be written in any subject.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Creative Writing with Reflection
topics.nameDe: Gestaltendes Schreiben zu literarischen Vorlagen mit Reflexion
topics.description: Write a creative text that continues, rewrites or responds to a literary model (a missing scene, a letter between characters, a modern adaptation) with aesthetic awareness, and reflect in a commentary on how it corresponds to the original's language, period and meaning.
evidence: Imitate the style and period language of a model
Stay consistent with the original's characters and themes
Explain the interpretive decisions in a reflection
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes a missing letter in 'Die Leiden des jungen Werthers', does it sound like Werther and can they explain how it reflects their reading of the novel?
topics.laenderNotes: According to the KMK, purely creative writing is not an Abitur task type but may follow an analysis as a further task.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Oral Exam: Talk and Discussion
topics.description: Prepare and deliver a structured talk on a task within a fixed preparation time, then defend and extend it in an examination conversation on wider subject connections — the format of the oral Abitur exam.
evidence: Structure a talk from notes within the preparation time
Answer follow-up questions precisely and link them to wider topics
Use subject terminology confidently in free speech
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a mock oral exam, can {{name}} present a poem analysis from notes and then answer questions linking it to the period?
topics.laenderNotes: Several Länder offer a presentation-based exam (Präsentationsprüfung or Besondere Lernleistung) as the fifth Abitur component.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Fair and Unfair Communication
topics.nameDe: Faire und unfaire Kommunikation: Strategien erkennen
topics.description: Recognise strategies of unfair communication in discussions and talk shows — killer phrases, personal attacks, interrupting, false dilemmas, straw men — respond to them calmly and moderate discussions so that all positions are heard.
evidence: Name unfair strategies in a recorded discussion
Respond to an unfair attack with a fair counter-strategy
Moderate a discussion with balanced turns
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a talk show, can they name the unfair tactics one guest uses and suggest how to respond?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Language as a Sign System
topics.nameDe: Sprache als Zeichensystem: Zeichenmodelle und Organon-Modell
topics.description: Describe language as a system of signs with Saussure's model (signifier and signified, arbitrariness, convention) and Bühler's Organon model (representation, expression, appeal), and distinguish the levels of language description: phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics.
evidence: Explain the arbitrariness of the sign with examples
Apply the Organon model to an utterance
Assign phenomena to the levels of language description
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why 'Baum', 'tree' and 'arbre' show that the link between word and thing is arbitrary?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Communication Models: Watzlawick
topics.description: Analyse communication in everyday and literary dialogues with Watzlawick's five axioms (one cannot not communicate, content and relationship, punctuation, digital and analogue, symmetrical and complementary) and compare the model with Schulz von Thun's.
evidence: Explain the five axioms with examples
Analyse a literary dialogue with the axioms
Compare Watzlawick's and Schulz von Thun's models
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} analyses a quarrel scene in a drama, can they explain its escalation with the axiom of punctuation?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Conversation Analysis and Power
topics.description: Analyse transcripts of conversations and literary dialogues — turn-taking, interruptions, question–answer patterns, register, verbal, paraverbal and nonverbal signals — and show how they reveal symmetrical or asymmetrical relationships and power.
evidence: Analyse turn-taking and interruptions in a transcript
Identify verbal and nonverbal signals of dominance
Explain the power relation in a dialogue
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads a transcript of a job interview or a doctor's visit, can they show how the conversation reveals who holds power?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Speech Act Theory
topics.description: Describe utterances as actions with speech act theory — locution, illocution and perlocution (Austin), Searle's classes of speech acts and indirect speech acts — and use these categories to analyse authentic and literary communication.
evidence: Classify utterances by Searle's classes of speech acts
Explain an indirect speech act
Analyse a dialogue with speech act categories
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why 'Es zieht' can be a request to close the window and name the speech act involved?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Analysing Political Speeches
topics.description: Analyse political and public speeches with rhetorical categories — situation, speaker and audience, ethos, pathos and logos, structure, rhetorical figures and persuasive strategies — and evaluate their effect and legitimacy, e.g. Richard von Weizsäcker's speech of 8 May 1985 or historical speeches.
evidence: Describe the speech situation and the audience
Analyse ethos, pathos and logos in a speech
Evaluate the speech's persuasive strategies critically
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} analyses Weizsäcker's speech of 8 May 1985, can they explain how he persuades his audience and why the speech was so influential?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
externalPrerequisites.concept: political communication and the role of speeches in democracy

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Steering Thought Through Language
topics.nameDe: Sprachlenkung: Framing, Schlagwörter und Sprache im Nationalsozialismus
topics.description: Analyse how word choice steers thinking in public discourse — framing (e.g. 'Steuerlast'), political slogans and euphemisms — with the language of National Socialism (Victor Klemperer's 'LTI') as a historical example of systematic language manipulation.
evidence: Explain framing with current examples
Analyse features of Nazi language with Klemperer
Evaluate the power and limits of steering through language
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why 'Steuerlast' and 'Steuerbeitrag' frame the same thing differently and compare this with Klemperer's observations?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Trends in Present-Day German
topics.description: Describe and evaluate current developments of German — Anglicisms, digital writing, simplification, gender-fair language, Kiezdeutsch — on the basis of language-critical texts, distinguishing descriptive linguistics from normative complaints about 'language decline'.
evidence: Describe a current trend with examples
Analyse the argument of a language-critical text
Distinguish descriptive and normative views of language change
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads an article claiming that German is 'in decline', can they analyse its arguments and respond from a linguistic point of view?
topics.laenderNotes: Niedersachsen: compulsory module 'Tendenzen in der deutschen Gegenwartssprache'.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Steered and Natural Language Change
topics.description: Distinguish natural (ungesteuert) language change from deliberate intervention (gesteuert): standardisation (Luther, Duden, spelling reforms), language societies and purism, language policy and guidelines — and assess how effective such steering is.
evidence: Give examples of natural and steered change
Explain the role of the Duden and the spelling reform
Assess arguments for and against regulating language
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between how 'Handy' entered German and how the 1996 spelling reform changed 'daß' to 'dass'?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Explaining Language Change
topics.description: Explain language change with linguistic theories — e.g. Rudi Keller's 'invisible hand', economy and expressiveness, language contact, grammaticalisation — and apply them to examples such as the decline of the genitive or the spread of Anglicisms.
evidence: Explain the invisible-hand theory
Apply a theory to a concrete change
Compare two explanations of the same change
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use Keller's theory to explain why 'wegen dem' spreads although many people criticise it?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Varieties and Social Meaning
topics.nameDe: Sprachvarietäten und ihre gesellschaftliche Bedeutung (Soziolekt, Dialekt)
topics.description: Compare varieties of German — dialects and regional languages (including Niederdeutsch), sociolects, youth language, technical languages — describe their features and functions and judge their social prestige and their role for identity.
evidence: Describe features of a dialect or sociolect
Explain the identity function of a variety
Discuss attitudes towards dialect speakers
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a strong regional accent may be valued at home but judged negatively in a job interview elsewhere?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Multilingualism and Language Contact
topics.description: Analyse individual and societal multilingualism in Germany: code-switching, ethnolects such as Kiezdeutsch, heritage languages and their status, and the effects of language contact on German.
evidence: Describe code-switching in a transcript
Explain features of Kiezdeutsch
Discuss the status of heritage languages in school and society
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain whether Kiezdeutsch is 'bad German' or a variety with its own rules?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: First Language Acquisition
topics.description: Describe the phases of first language acquisition (babbling, one-word and two-word stage, telegraphic speech, overgeneralisation such as 'gegeht') and the conditions that support it, using transcripts of child language.
evidence: Order the phases of language acquisition with examples
Explain overgeneralisation errors
Analyse a transcript of child language
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears a three-year-old say 'Ich habe gegeht', can they explain why this 'mistake' shows learning?

prerequisites.reason: Strong and weak verbs explain overgeneralisation

topics.laenderNotes: Placement differs: Grundkurs in NRW (2014 plan) and as an elective module in Niedersachsen; Leistungskurs only in the new NRW plan (from 2027) and theory-based only for eA in the KMK standards.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Theories of Language Acquisition
topics.description: Compare theories of language acquisition — behaviourism (Skinner), nativism (Chomsky's language acquisition device), cognitivism (Piaget) and interactionism (Bruner) — and test them against evidence such as overgeneralisation or cases of language deprivation.
evidence: Summarise the core assumptions of three theories
Test a theory against a piece of evidence
Evaluate which theory explains acquisition best
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why children's overgeneralisations are a problem for behaviourism but support Chomsky's view?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Language, Thought and Reality
topics.description: Discuss the relationship between language, thought and reality: Humboldt's idea of language as a world view, the strong and weak Sapir–Whorf hypothesis (linguistic relativity) and universalist counter-positions, tested against examples such as colour terms or grammatical gender.
evidence: Explain the strong and the weak version of linguistic relativity
Evaluate an empirical example
Take a reasoned position in the debate
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain whether speakers of a language with many words for snow actually perceive snow differently?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW: Grundkurs in the new plan (from 2027), before only Leistungskurs; Niedersachsen: elective module; KMK names positions from the philosophy of language for eA.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Language Scepticism
topics.description: Analyse philosophical and literary expressions of scepticism about language — Nietzsche's 'Über Wahrheit und Lüge im außermoralischen Sinne', Hofmannsthal's Chandos-Brief, Wittgenstein's limits of language — and relate them to literary works of the Moderne.
evidence: Summarise Nietzsche's critique of concepts
Relate the Chandos-Brief to a philosophical position
Discuss the limits of language with reference to Wittgenstein
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain Nietzsche's claim that truths are 'worn-out metaphors' and connect it to the language crisis around 1900?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Religion & Ethik
externalPrerequisites.concept: Nietzsche's philosophy and his critique of metaphysics

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the subjunctive (Konjunktiv I and II) for reported speech, wishes and unreal conditions, the forms of the passive, and how subordinate clauses and infinitive or participle groups work as parts of a sentence — and how linking words hold a text together.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt den Konjunktiv I und II für indirekte Rede, Wünsche und Irreales, die Formen des Passivs und wie Nebensätze sowie Infinitiv- und Partizipgruppen als Satzglieder wirken — und wie Verknüpfungswörter einen Text zusammenhalten.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to recognise and use the nominal style of official and academic German and to judge when plain verbal style is easier to understand.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt den Nominalstil der Amts- und Wissenschaftssprache zu erkennen und zu verwenden und einzuschätzen, wann ein verbaler Stil verständlicher ist.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning that words carry more than their core meaning: connotations can make the same thing sound neutral, positive or negative, and writers use this to steer readers.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, dass Wörter mehr transportieren als ihre Grundbedeutung: Konnotationen lassen dieselbe Sache neutral, positiv oder abwertend klingen, und Texte nutzen das zur Lenkung der Leser.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the harder comma rules (infinitive and participle groups, aber/sondern, als/wie), when words are written together or apart, how to use semicolon, colon and dash, and how to spell loanwords of Greek and Latin origin.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die schwierigeren Kommaregeln (Infinitiv- und Partizipgruppen, aber/sondern, als/wie), die Getrennt- und Zusammenschreibung, den Gebrauch von Semikolon, Doppelpunkt und Gedankenstrich sowie die Schreibung griechischer und lateinischer Fremdwörter.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to settle doubtful cases of spelling independently by checking the official rules or a dictionary and explaining the decision.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, orthografische Zweifelsfälle selbstständig mithilfe des amtlichen Regelwerks oder eines Wörterbuchs zu klären und die Entscheidung zu begründen.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning school writing genres that last until the Abitur: the formal plot summary (Inhaltsangabe), character analysis, a first argumentative essay, letters to the editor and commentaries, minutes, correct quoting and a structured literary analysis.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt Schreibformen, die bis zum Abitur tragen: Inhaltsangabe, Figurencharakteristik, die erste (lineare) Erörterung, Leserbrief und Kommentar, Protokoll, korrektes Zitieren und eine gegliederte Textanalyse.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to weigh pros and cons in a dialectical essay, judge the strength of arguments, write arguments based on materials, and write a job application and CV, often around the work placement.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, in der dialektischen Erörterung Pro und Kontra abzuwägen, die Stichhaltigkeit von Argumenten zu beurteilen, materialgestützt zu argumentieren und — oft rund um das Betriebspraktikum — Bewerbung und Lebenslauf zu schreiben.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is practising the Abitur task types — interpreting literary texts, analysing and discussing non-fiction texts, writing informative or argumentative texts from a dossier of materials — as well as the essay, reviews and an academic-style Facharbeit.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind übt die Aufgabenarten des Abiturs — Interpretation literarischer Texte, Analyse und Erörterung pragmatischer Texte, materialgestütztes informierendes und argumentierendes Schreiben — sowie Essay, Rezension und eine wissenschaftspropädeutische Facharbeit.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to read several sources on one topic side by side, compare what they say and judge which ones are reliable.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, mehrere Quellen zu einem Thema vergleichend zu lesen, ihre Aussagen gegenüberzustellen und ihre Verlässlichkeit einzuschätzen.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to excerpt texts for a question, with page numbers and sources, as preparation for presentations and longer papers.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Texte für eine Fragestellung zu exzerpieren — mit Seitenangaben und Quellen — als Vorbereitung auf Referate und längere Arbeiten.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the tools of literary analysis — narrative mode and time, ballads, short stories and drama scenes, poetry analysis and rhetorical devices — and analyses films, newspapers and advertising.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt das Handwerkszeug der Textanalyse — Erzählverhalten und Zeitgestaltung, Ballade, Kurzgeschichte und Dramenszene, Gedichtanalyse und Stilmittel — und untersucht Filme, Zeitungstexte und Werbung.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is reading longer and older works — novellas, a novel, a classical drama, parables — interpreting motifs and symbols in their historical context, comparing texts and analysing argumentative texts and online disinformation.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind liest längere und ältere Werke — Novelle, Roman, klassisches Drama, Parabel —, deutet Motive und Symbole im historischen Kontext, vergleicht Texte und analysiert argumentierende Sachtexte und Desinformation im Netz.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is interpreting prose, drama and poetry with specialist categories, comparing texts across periods, judging film adaptations and stage productions, and — in the Leistungskurs — working with literary and media theory.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind interpretiert Epik, Dramatik und Lyrik mit Fachkategorien, vergleicht Texte über Epochen hinweg, beurteilt Verfilmungen und Inszenierungen und arbeitet im Leistungskurs zusätzlich mit Literatur- und Medientheorie.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to support presentations with clear slides and handouts and to explore literary texts through drama methods such as freeze frames and role biographies.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Präsentationen mit klaren Folien und Handouts zu unterstützen und literarische Texte szenisch zu interpretieren, etwa mit Standbildern und Rollenbiografien.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to write and give a persuasive speech, to debate in a fixed format and to prepare for job interviews.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, eine überzeugende Rede zu verfassen und zu halten, in festem Format zu debattieren und sich auf Vorstellungsgespräche vorzubereiten.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning to spot unfair tactics in discussions and to prepare for the oral Abitur: a prepared talk followed by an examination conversation.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, unfaire Strategien in Diskussionen zu erkennen, und bereitet sich auf die mündliche Abiturprüfung vor: einen vorbereiteten Vortrag mit anschließendem Prüfungsgespräch.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is examining youth language as a variety of German and analysing misunderstandings with the four-sides model of communication.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind untersucht Jugendsprache als Varietät des Deutschen und analysiert Missverständnisse mit dem Kommunikationsquadrat.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how German has changed since the Middle Ages, how language can discriminate or manipulate, how gender-fair wording works and why a chat can be written yet 'spoken' in style.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie sich das Deutsche seit dem Mittelalter verändert hat, wie Sprache diskriminieren oder manipulieren kann, wie geschlechtergerechte Formulierungen funktionieren und warum ein Chat zwar geschrieben, aber konzeptionell mündlich ist.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is meeting the first literary period in depth, the Enlightenment, usually through a play by Lessing and the ideas of reason and tolerance.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt mit der Aufklärung die erste literarische Epoche gründlich kennen, meist an einem Drama Lessings und an den Ideen von Vernunft und Toleranz.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is travelling through German literary history from the Baroque and Sturm und Drang via Klassik, Romantik and the Moderne to post-war and contemporary literature, linking texts to their time.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind geht durch die deutsche Literaturgeschichte vom Barock und Sturm und Drang über Klassik, Romantik und Moderne bis zur Nachkriegs- und Gegenwartsliteratur und verbindet Texte mit ihrer Zeit.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is studying language itself: signs and communication models, power in conversation, political rhetoric and framing, language change and varieties, and — in the Leistungskurs — theories of language acquisition and the philosophy of language.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind beschäftigt sich mit Sprache selbst: Zeichen- und Kommunikationsmodelle, Macht im Gespräch, politische Rhetorik und Framing, Sprachwandel und Varietäten sowie im Leistungskurs Spracherwerbstheorien und Sprachphilosophie.
